Links: [{"title":"www.mintlify.com","url":"https://www.mintlify.com/cloudflare/workers-sdk/advanced/assets"},{"title":"developers.webflow.com","url":"https://developers.webflow.com/webflow-cloud/environment/configuration"},{"title":"static assets","url":"https://docs.cloudflare.com/workers/vite-plugin/reference/static-assets/"},{"title":"Configuration and Bindings","url":"https://docs.cloudflare.com/workers/static-assets/binding/"},{"title":"Serving a subdirectory","url":"https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/static-assets/routing/advanced/serving-a-subdirectory/"},{"title":"developers.cloudflare.com","url":"https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/static-assets/index.md"},{"title":"Awesome-omni-skill preferences-cloudflare-wrangler-reference","url":"https://openskillindex.com/skills/diegosouzapw-awesome-omni-skill-preferences-cloudflare-wrangler-reference"},{"title":"docs-durable-objects-instance-replaced-errors.previews.developers.cloudflare.com","url":"https://docs-durable-objects-instance-replaced-errors.previews.developers.cloudflare.com/workers/static-assets/routing/advanced/serving-a-subdirectory/index.md"},{"title":"439c4358.previews.developers.cloudflare.com","url":"https://439c4358.previews.developers.cloudflare.com/workers/static-assets/binding/index.md"},{"title":"serving a subdirectory","url":"https://69edd8d5.previews.developers.cloudflare.com/workers/static-assets/routing/advanced/serving-a-subdirectory/"}]

The main approach in Cloudflare's docs is to mirror the path in your asset folder and then bind the Worker to that path with a route. The search didn't turn up a separate base-path or prefix setting in the Wrangler `assets` block.

**Mirror the path in the directory tree.** The official subdirectory guide says assets must sit in a folder structure that matches the target path. For example.com/blog/*, you create a blog directory in your asset directory. So a `dist/blog/index.html` file and a `dist/blog/posts/` folder would cover that prefix.

**Add a route and point `assets` at the folder.** The example config sets a `route` of `example.com/blog/*` alongside `"assets": { "directory": "dist" }`. With that setup, requests to example.com/blog/ will serve the index.html file, and requests to example.com/blog/posts/post1 will serve the post1.html file.

**Version requirement.** The subdirectory page notes that this feature requires Wrangler v3.98.0 or later. Older Wrangler versions may not support this pattern.

**Other relevant settings:**
- **Worker-first routing:** If a Worker should handle some paths under the prefix, run_worker_first = false (default) will serve any static asset matching a request, while run_worker_first = true will unconditionally invoke your Worker script. A pattern list such as `/api/*` also works for targeted cases.
- **Excluding files:** A `.assetsignore` file in the asset root uses the same format as .gitignore. Matching files are not uploaded.
- **Single-page apps:** For client-side routing under a prefix, the `not_found_handling` option controls what happens when no asset matches. The Vite plugin docs show an example setting it to the single-page-application fallback, so the fallback will always be the root index.html file.

If you're using a framework such as Vite, Next.js, or Astro, check that framework's own base-path setting first, since it may generate the `wrangler.json` for you. The Webflow Cloud docs, for example, generate a wrangler.json configuration file based on the framework specified during deployment.
